detection.summary: Java EE 7 monolith application running on WebLogic with WAR packaging

language.name: Java
language.reasoning: Quarkus 3 requires Java 17 minimum. Choosing Java 17 LTS for stability and conservative migration approach.

packaging.reasoning: Fast-jar is Quarkus default, optimized for container deployment with faster startup than uber-jar

custom_libraries.issue: System-scoped dependencies not recommended for Quarkus

decisions.question: Which Java LTS version should be the migration target?

options.label: Java 17 (LTS)
options.description: Minimum requirement for Quarkus 3, well-tested, conservative

options.label: Java 21 (LTS)
options.description: Latest LTS with newest features, longer support timeline

decisions.reasoning: Java 17 is the minimum requirement and most conservative choice. The codebase doesn't require Java 21 features, and Java 17 minimizes migration risk while providing all necessary Quarkus 3 support.

decisions.question: Which messaging backend should replace JMS?

options.label: Apache Kafka with SmallRye Reactive Messaging
options.description: Production-grade, scalable, event streaming platform

options.label: AMQP (ActiveMQ Artemis) with SmallRye Reactive Messaging
options.description: JMS-like semantics, easier migration from JMS Topics

options.label: In-memory channels
options.description: Simple, no external dependencies, development/testing only

decisions.reasoning: AMQP with ActiveMQ Artemis provides the closest semantics to JMS Topics used in the application. It's the Red Hat/JBoss recommended broker and simplifies migration from the existing JMS pub/sub pattern. Kafka would require more architectural changes.

decisions.question: How should database migrations be handled?

options.label: Keep existing Flyway with manual configuration
options.description: Minimal changes, continue using existing SQL migrations

options.label: Use Quarkus Flyway extension
options.description: Better integration, automatic migration, native support

options.label: Migrate to Liquibase
options.description: Different tool, requires rewriting migrations

decisions.reasoning: Quarkus Flyway extension reuses existing SQL migration files while providing seamless Quarkus integration, automatic execution on startup, and native compilation support. No migration file changes needed.

decisions.question: How should the @Remote EJB (ShippingService) be handled?

options.label: Convert to REST endpoint
options.description: HTTP-based, widely compatible, uses existing REST infrastructure

options.label: Use Quarkus gRPC
options.description: Efficient binary protocol, typed interfaces, more setup required

options.label: Make local-only (remove remote capability)
options.description: Simplest if no remote consumers exist

decisions.reasoning: REST endpoint maintains remote access capability using standard HTTP protocols. The application already has REST infrastructure in place. This provides maximum flexibility and compatibility without requiring new protocols like gRPC.

decisions.question: How should session state be managed (CartEndpoint is @SessionScoped, ShoppingCartService is @Stateful)?

options.label: Keep Quarkus session-scoped beans
options.description: Easiest migration, requires sticky sessions in production

options.label: Stateless with JWT tokens
options.description: Cloud-native, scalable, requires frontend changes

options.label: Redis/database session store
options.description: Scalable, shared sessions, adds external dependency

decisions.reasoning: To minimize initial migration scope, preserve session-scoped beans to maintain existing behavior. This avoids frontend changes. For production cloud deployment, document JWT-based stateless authentication as a future enhancement. Provides clear migration path without blocking Quarkus migration.
decisions.future_recommendation: Migrate to JWT-based stateless authentication for cloud-native scalability
decisions.production_consideration: Requires sticky sessions or session replication

decisions.question: How should WebLogic ApplicationLifecycleListener be replaced?

options.label: Quarkus lifecycle events (@Observes StartupEvent/ShutdownEvent)
options.description: Quarkus-native, clean, simple

options.label: CDI lifecycle events (@Observes @Initialized)
options.description: Portable CDI-standard approach

options.label: Remove if not essential
options.description: Current listener only logs, may not be needed

decisions.reasoning: Quarkus lifecycle events are the idiomatic approach with clear semantics. The current listener only performs logging, making this a straightforward conversion. Easy to implement and test.

decisions.question: What packaging format should be used for deployment?

options.label: Fast-jar (Quarkus default)
options.description: Optimized startup, smaller size, multiple files

options.label: Uber-jar
options.description: Single JAR file, traditional, larger size

options.label: Native executable
options.description: Fastest startup, smallest memory, long build times

decisions.reasoning: Fast-jar is the Quarkus default and recommended for containerized deployments. It provides the best balance of startup time and deployment size. Native compilation can be evaluated later if extreme startup speed is needed.

decisions.question: How should the system-scoped audit-logging-library be handled?

options.label: Install to local Maven repository
options.description: Proper Maven dependency management, better portability

options.label: Use Maven Central or corporate repository
options.description: Cleanest approach if artifact is available

options.label: Examine and potentially inline
options.description: Most control, only if library is simple

decisions.reasoning: System-scoped dependencies don't work well with Quarkus. Installing the JAR to the local Maven repository maintains the dependency while improving build portability. Without access to a corporate Maven repository, this is the safest intermediate step.

phases.name: Build Config
phases.description: Restructure pom.xml: WAR→JAR, add Quarkus BOM and plugin, replace Java EE dependencies with Quarkus extensions

phases.name: App Config
phases.description: Replace persistence.xml with application.properties, remove web.xml and beans.xml

phases.name: EJB to CDI
phases.description: Replace EJB annotations with CDI, remove Remote/Local interfaces, replace JNDI lookups with injection

phases.name: Messaging
phases.description: Convert MDB classes to SmallRye Reactive Messaging, replace JMS producers with Emitter

phases.name: Lifecycle
phases.description: Replace server-specific lifecycle listeners with Quarkus startup/shutdown events

phases.name: Cleanup
phases.description: Delete legacy files, remove weblogic/jboss stubs, verify no javax.* EE imports remain

prerequisites: Install audit-logging-library to local Maven repository
Set up ActiveMQ Artemis broker for testing
Verify current application builds successfully on Java EE

risks.description: Session state migration may affect user experience if sticky sessions not configured
risks.mitigation: Test session behavior thoroughly, configure load balancer for sticky sessions

risks.description: JMS to AMQP migration may have message format incompatibilities
risks.mitigation: Create integration tests for message flow, verify Order serialization/deserialization

risks.description: WebLogic-specific JNDI lookups need complete replacement
risks.mitigation: Map all JNDI names to Quarkus configuration, test all injection points

risks.description: Remote EJB clients may exist outside the codebase
risks.mitigation: Document REST endpoint as replacement, provide migration guide for clients

datasource.notes: Database type needs to be determined (defaulting to PostgreSQL based on common JBoss setup)

jms_topic.notes: Configure AMQP connector for ActiveMQ Artemis

success_criteria: Application builds successfully with 'mvn clean package'
Messages are published and consumed via AMQP
No javax.* EE imports remain in codebase
test_strategy: Run existing unit tests with Quarkus Test framework
Create integration tests for REST endpoints
Verify database schema and data migrations
